what: the GitHub token can do far more than the lab needs - delete repositories, administer organizations and the enterprise - so whoever holds it can do all of that
the GitHub token appeared in process listings and in conversation; it must be rotated
countermeasure: rotated 2026-11-12 by the author. The new token reached the lab sealed with a one-time key made on the lab (RSA-OAEP), never in the jobs repository; installed in its two places (token, env), the voice and oco-agent restarted onto it, and the work landed through it. The assistant's helpers read it from a private file, no longer written into commands. The old token is kept aside, private, until the author revokes it.

what: the watcher's schedule ran once, nine hours late, then not again: GitHub's schedules are best-effort and drop silently
countermeasure: the pulse at Healthchecks is the lab's watcher; the workflow is a probe run by hand (decisions:2026-11-12-the-pulse-is-the-watcher). Its alerts reach the author's email; through ntfy once the author adds that integration in Healthchecks.
